summary_paragraph: A male patient with a history of Factor V Leiden deficiency, chronic anticoagulation with Lovenox, prior pulmonary embolism, and aortic arch thrombus was admitted for recurrent atypical chest pain. The pain was mid-sternal, dull, and pressure-like, unchanged from prior admissions. Evaluation showed normal cardiac enzymes, a benign EKG, and a clear chest X-ray with no acute findings. Given recent imaging and stable vital signs, no additional CT was performed. The pain was attributed to musculoskeletal causes, and the patient was managed without additional narcotics per his contract. He was advised to restart tizanidine, use over-the-counter NSAIDs, and continue all home medications, especially Lovenox. The patient declined psychiatric follow-up despite ongoing chronic pain and anxiety. He was discharged home in stable condition with instructions to follow up with his primary care provider.
